subject.title: feat(cli): `skills uninstall` design proposal + prior art reconciliation

question: Should OpenClaw add a destructive `openclaw skills uninstall <slug>` CLI now, and if so should it remove only ClawHub-tracked installs or also manual/git/local skill directories?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but removing workspace files is a product/security contract and the issue explicitly leaves manual-skill, global/agent, dry-run, and CLI-versus-Gateway semantics for maintainer choice.

options.title: Approve narrow ClawHub CLI uninstall
options.body: Add a CLI command that removes a safe-resolved selected skills directory plus the matching ClawHub lock/origin metadata, with confirmation, dry-run, JSON, and regression tests for stale lockfile cleanup.

options.title: Prefer Gateway lifecycle first
options.body: Keep the CLI issue open but ask for a Gateway-owned uninstall API first so dashboard/operator surfaces and CLI share one backend contract.

options.title: Defer destructive uninstall
options.body: Leave manual deletion and current update behavior as-is until maintainers want a broader skill lifecycle redesign.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow ClawHub CLI uninstall
recommendation.body: Add a CLI command that removes a safe-resolved selected skills directory plus the matching ClawHub lock/origin metadata, with confirmation, dry-run, JSON, and regression tests for stale lockfile cleanup.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter introduced both the skills CLI and native ClawHub install lifecycle, making him the best available routing owner for this product/API shape decision.
